title: Here is The Trailer for My Game, Heavy Mental—inspired by Metal Slug and Developed Entirely on My Own Over The Past Year...
author: Basic-Campaign-774
selftext:
What do you think, friends?

To add it to your wishlist on Steam...

[Steam Page](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4532680/Heavy_Mental_A_Coop_Action_Roguelite/)

comments.author: songokuthegreat
comments.body: This is extremely impressive! My only concern is in regards to the inconsistency when it comes to the frame rate. But nice job overall. Look forward to playing this.

replies.author: Basic-Campaign-774
replies.body: Thanks, my friend; by the way, there are quite a lot of surprise characters in the game... :)

comments.author: Wooden_Plant7504
comments.body: Very good looking! I like it. Care to share a bit about your workflow ? Especially what you used for character design/modelling ?

replies.author: Basic-Campaign-774
replies.body: I used Hunyuan 3d 3.1 and Blender my friend...

replies.author: Wooden_Plant7504
replies.body: Thanks for your answer. It looks great

comments.author: RepulsiveRaisin7
comments.body: That looks like textbook slop to me, I don't like it. So many things lack polish and the trailer is lagging.

replies.author: Basic-Campaign-774
replies.body: No matter what you do, there are some people you can never please; they always find fault with everything... Unfortunately, that’s because their perspective is always a negative one.

replies.author: Wooden_Plant7504
replies.body: Why'd you remove it ? It was good...

replies.author: Basic-Campaign-774
replies.body: I’m fed up with people whose whole life consists of nothing but criticizing everyone, my friend—unfortunately...

replies.author: Wooden_Plant7504
replies.body:
Well... the criticism is unqualified and unspecific, so you could ignore it...  
This reminds me of someone I know who criticised one of the first popular albums of Bruno Mars when it came out a while back. He was saying that to him, Mars was an obvious copycat of Michael Jackson and that there was just 'something that didn't feel right' with Mars, going on about how imperfect he was...  
That didn't stop me (and probably a few others) from paying top dollar to go see Mars later on.  
Not saying your stuff was at that level of talent, but besides looking like you were influenced by a game style, it didn't look like slop at all to me.

You can put anything in endless loops of improvements and adjustments. Including people's pretend moral and ethical values.

Anyway. Good luck with your work.

replies.author: RepulsiveRaisin7
replies.body: You guys are delusional. I don't really need to explain my critique frame by frame, I'm not paid to give people feedback. The darn trailer was lagging, do you really need to know more at that point? Gamers will rip this to shreds. I have complimented many games here, saying I hate everything is such a lazy and nonsensical response

replies.author: Wooden_Plant7504
replies.body:
You might want to read your post again and consider you may have been a tad hostile.   
I don't think anyone offered to pay you for feedback, whoever you or your qualifications may be.   
I just think that in an "ai game dev" forum you might want to make so called 'criticism' constructive, or give helpful pointers to contribute positively to the conversation.   
Otherwise why even bother commenting if only to pretend being a member of the anti-slop police.  
"Gamers will rip that to shreds"... that is the delusion... you don't have a crystal ball, or fingers on the pulse of the global gaming community.  
  
You might pretend you wanted to be helpful but apparently you weren't.  
  
I am a gamer, and I have played and paid for hundreds of games...  
  
I was interested in checking that guy's game out, and at least have the opportunity to see what it looks like without him retreating in the shadows because he experienced Vogsphere...

replies.author: RepulsiveRaisin7
replies.body: OP could've just asked if they wanted to know more. I'm repeating myself but a lagging trailer is a big fucking deal, so that's helpful already. Arguably more helpful than comments telling them they made the best thing ever. But OP is crying in a corner because of one negative comment. They're never gonna make it

replies.author: Wooden_Plant7504
replies.body:
Dunno about you. But if I got a comment like yours I wouldn't "just ask to know more". I would tell myself that I don't know who you are or what on earth makes you qualified to give one liner hostile feedback or claim to read the future and people's minds.  
Statements like "They're never gonna make it" are plain ridiculous in this day and age...  
I am not sure that's the person you really want to be but hey...all the best to you and your projects.

replies.author: RepulsiveRaisin7
replies.body: Selling games is an uphill battle, 97% of games get fewer than 1k reviews on Steam. If you can't learn from feedback, I think your chances of success are genuinely close to zero. That's not me being rude, that's reality.

replies.author: Wooden_Plant7504
replies.body:
I think I understand the underlying burn-out, "life is tough kiddo" message you are saying you'd like to convey. Yet I persist in thinking this approach sounds a bit all-knowing and dogmatic coming from an anonymous redditor. It is also without any positive effect.   
I think giving constructive and helpful feedback is a skill. One you could very well attempt to learn from this feedback...

replies.author: RepulsiveRaisin7
replies.body: Well good luck if this is your response to criticism. Gamers will not respond kindly to this.

comments.author: Upper-Philosophy2376
comments.body: gameplay looks really fun, character cards and similar artwork still have an AI smell to them.
